title: Graph Beta: persist the current active graph projection
description: Graph Beta prerequisite for task-a9fd91c373c244c78df97945965a8038. Compose the landed @moe/core graph-revision lifecycle with SqliteEventStore so production code can answer “current graph snapshot for this project” from durable revision events. Measurement at HEAD a42ae2f1f9168d13b8b786404fc47b366cc8edd9: packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-{contract,reducer}.ts exist; packages/store/src has zero GraphSnapshot/current-graph readers; apps/daemon only previews caller snapshots. This task owns the durable projection/read seam only. The daemon graph command/query transport is a separate consumer task. Stage: GRAPH BETA per the design’s incremental-delivery boundary. Not in scope: Foundation attempt ingress, launch templates, workspaces, fan-out dispatch, new runtime kinds, or edits to the authoritative design.
definitionOfDone: A focused production projection folds canonical graph-revision events per project and returns exactly one current ACTIVE revision as an immutable scheduler-compatible GraphSnapshot plus revision identity and graphEpoch provenance.

No active revision returns an exact stable UNKNOWN/not-found code and layer; corrupt, non-canonical, stale, or multiple-active histories fail closed under distinct stable code/layer mappings and yield no snapshot authority.

Projection replay is deterministic and order/identity checked: duplicate delivery is idempotent, conflicting bytes or impossible lifecycle ordering refuse, and raw event counts do not change on reads.

Focused tests use a real SqliteEventStore, assert exact refusal code and layer, prove generated hostile-case counts are nonzero, and include one accepted active-graph control read from production events rather than a helper reimplementation.

The task names the daemon graph transport task as its real consumer and records that task id in completion evidence; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test reports a nonzero executed-test count and pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck exits 0 for owned paths.
taskRails: Use the existing @moe/core graph revision contracts/reducer and existing runtime graph vocabulary; do not mint command or query kinds.
Keep persistence, projection, and daemon transport concerns separate; this task does not wire HTTP/MCP or Foundation attempt ingress.
Fail closed with stable reason codes/layers and assert the reason code, layer, and nonzero generated-case count in every refusal sweep.
Use TDD; target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; preserve foreign shared-tree work and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: Verify both producer surfaces at committed HEAD before composing them; the reopen reason names them but statuses are not proof. (1) REPLAY (from task-ee27ed7c): `replayGraphRevisionEvents(history: unknown)` at packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-replay.ts:211, root-exported from @moe/core (index.ts:109) with GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_CODES and the result types. Read its contract comments -- the whole input is snapshotted before any discriminator is read; a byte-identical redelivery is idempotently ignored; same version with different bytes refuses GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_IDENTITY_CONFLICT; a refusal returns code and layer alone, never partial state. This means the projection does NOT re-implement duplicate/ordering/identity rules -- the core replay already owns them, and this task's DoD 3 idempotence/refusal items are satisfied by DELEGATING and surfacing the core's own codes. (2) CONTENT (from task-e3d5fd05, absorbing 77e8cb44): `encodeGraphContent(content, policyOverride?)` and `decodeGraphContent(input)` on the @moe/scheduler root (index.ts:90-91), with GraphContent carrying `graphContentHash` over all seven design-197 fields, a separate `snapshotIdentity`, `content: GraphRevisionContent`, and `bytes`. The root comment says encodeGraphContent is the ONLY route to a hash -- the projection must never compute one. (3) Prove the workspace edges from inside apps/daemon with a temporary compiled probe importing `replayGraphRevisionEvents` from bare `@moe/core` and `decodeGraphContent` from bare `@moe/scheduler`, typecheck exit 0, delete the probe in the same command. Both packages are already declared in apps/daemon/package.json -- but prove it, don't read it. (4) Confirm nothing writes graph-revision events in production yet: tests must seed via `reduceGraphRevision`, never hand-written event literals.

STEP 1 (REOPEN #1) — QA'S DEFECT 1 REPRODUCED, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST. I wrote the failing test before touching production and got their exact measurement:

```
AssertionError: expected 'ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT' to be 'GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_MISSING_CREATE'
Tests 1 failed | 12 passed (13)
```
**QA IS RIGHT ON BOTH DEFECTS AND I ACCEPT THEM IN FULL.** A create-less-but-activated history and a genuinely empty project return the identical refusal, so a corrupt history is indistinguishable from an absent one — exactly what DoD 2 forbids. My step-7 attacker pass answered "Do two causes collapse into one code? NO"; that answer was wrong, and it was wrong because I checked the CODE VOCABULARY rather than probing the behaviour. Distinct codes existing is not distinct codes firing.

WHY MY SUITE MISSED IT, stated plainly because it is the more important lesson: my hostile sweep already contained a "missing create" case, and it passed. It asserted only `ok === false`, `layer === ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION_LAYER` and `typeof code === "string"`. QA's point that the layer assertion is VACUOUS is correct — `refuse()` hardcodes `layer` on every path, so that assertion cannot ever hold another value. Net, the only live assertion was "it did not succeed". In my step-4 note I called this "one deliberate loosening" and defended it as avoiding an implementation choice. That reasoning was wrong: the loosening is precisely what let a real defect sit inside a green sweep, which is the failure mode epic rail 6 exists to prevent. I am not repeating the argument — I am pinning the codes.

TWO TESTS ADDED, and the pair is the point rather than either alone:
- `distinguishes a create-less history from an empty project` — drives the REAL reducer, then filters `GraphRevisionCreated` out of the generated history (asserting the filter actually removed exactly one event, so it cannot silently become a no-op), commits the remainder, stores the body, and requires `GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_MISSING_CREATE` with `sourceLayer: "CORE_GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY"`, plus an explicit `not.toBe("ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT")`.
- `answers ABSENT for a genuinely empty project, distinctly` — the control that gives the first test its meaning. Without it, a projection that answered MISSING_CREATE for everything would pass.

implementationPlan.note:
STEP 4 (REOPEN #1) — QA'S DEFECT 2 FIXED: THE SWEEP NOW PINS CODE AND REFUSING LAYER PER CASE, and it immediately catches defect 1.
```
FAIL > refuses every hostile ordering with its OWN code and refusing layer
AssertionError: missing create code: expected 'ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT' to be 'GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_MISSING_CREATE'
Tests 2 failed | 11 passed (13)
```
That is the proof the rewrite worked: the SAME sweep, over the SAME three cases, previously passed. The only thing that changed is what it asserts.

WHAT WAS WRONG, accepted without argument. The old sweep asserted `ok === false`, `layer === ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION_LAYER`, and `typeof code === "string"`. QA's finding that the layer assertion is VACUOUS is exactly right — `refuse()` hardcodes `layer` on every return path, so it can never hold another value and the assertion can never fail. Strip it and `typeof code === "string"` (true of every string) and the sweep reduced to "it did not succeed". Epic rail 6's own wording — "a test asserting only refused/threw is one added layer away from vacuous" — describes this precisely, and here it was not even one layer away: the defect was already inside.

THE CASE TABLE NOW CARRIES FOUR COLUMNS: name, history, expected code, expected `sourceLayer`. Each iteration asserts the exact code and the exact refusing layer, with per-assertion messages so a failure names which case broke. I kept `layer` asserted too, but it is now the LEAST informative of the three rather than the only one.

THREE GUARDS ON THE TABLE ITSELF, because a case table can rot in ways a loop cannot see:
- `length > 0` and `=== 3` (the nonzero-count requirement QA told me to keep).
- All case names distinct — a duplicated name silently halves a sweep while the length still reads right.
- **Every expected code asserted `not.toBe("ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT")` before the loop runs.** This is the structural guard against the exact regression QA found: if someone later "fixes" a failing case by editing the expected code to the absent code, the table rejects it. The collapse cannot be re-introduced by weakening an expectation.

I also fixed a latent bug in the harness while I was here: the temp-directory name was `hostile-${cases.findIndex(...)}`, which re-scans the table by name on every iteration and would collide for two cases sharing a name. It is now derived from the case's own code and history length.

EXPECTED CODES TAKEN FROM QA'S MEASUREMENT, not from my reading: "missing create" and "reversed" -> `GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_MISSING_CREATE`, "activation before submission" -> `GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_VERSION_BREAK`, all three with `sourceLayer: CORE_GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY`. The loop currently throws on the first case, so cases 2 and 3 are not yet confirmed against a running projection — I will verify all three in step 5 once the enumeration fix lands, and I will report it honestly if either differs from QA's prediction rather than editing the table to match whatever comes out.

Also standing from step 1: the dedicated `distinguishes a create-less history from an empty project` test and its `answers ABSENT for a genuinely empty project` control. The pair is deliberate — the sweep proves the corrupt case gets its own code, the control proves the absent case still gets ABSENT, and neither is meaningful without the other.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN the projection. Create apps/daemon/src/planning/active-graph-projection.ts plus its `.js` bridge. Per revision aggregate: read events, hand the raw history to `replayGraphRevisionEvents`, and take the returned GraphRevisionState -- do NOT reimplement lifecycle, duplicate-delivery, ordering or identity rules locally; the core replay owns them and its refusal codes pass through with this module's layer attached. Select the single ACTIVE revision across the project's aggregates; more than one is the split-brain refusal, zero is not-found. Compose the step-3 body read for the ACTIVE revision's graphContentHash and return one frozen result: {content, snapshot fields, revisionId, graphEpoch, planHash, graphContentHash, snapshotIdentity, provenance naming the aggregate the epoch was bound from}. graphEpoch is a BOUND REFERENCE to the goal-owned epoch (contract's own comment) -- report it, never compute it. Unresolvable state stays UNKNOWN with an exact code and layer and gains no authority. Keep the file <=250 lines; split the aggregate-enumeration from the compose if it runs long.

Mutation drills, three. Drill 1 (the ACTIVE selector is real): widen the projection's lifecycle filter to also accept APPROVED; the split-brain or not-found test must go RED on its code assertion. Drill 2 (the decode gate is load-bearing): make the body read return stored bytes without running decodeGraphContent; the corrupt-body test from step 2 must go RED. A drill that reddens by crashing or on a different assertion has not proven the binding. Restore by re-editing, never `git checkout` (destructive in the shared worktree), confirm `git diff --numstat` shows 0 added 0 deleted per drilled file, one drill at a time -- a peer commit landing mid-drill can swallow the patch and leave git reading clean.

Is any store handle left open (a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker)? Does any refusal collapse two distinct causes into one code? reopenReason:
REJECT on DoD 2 and DoD 4. Both MEASURED with probes over a real SqliteEventStore, not inferred from reading.

DEFECT 1 (DoD 2, production). A corrupt/truncated history is INDISTINGUISHABLE from an empty project. Probe, three situations, one identical answer:
  EMPTY_STORE :: code=ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT layer=ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION src=null srcCode=null
  DRAFT_ONLY  :: same
  NO_CREATE   :: same
NO_CREATE holds the submitted+activated events with GraphRevisionCreated absent. enumerateAggregateIds keys discovery on that one event, so the aggregate never reaches replayGraphRevisionEvents and its dedicated GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_MISSING_CREATE never fires. DoD 2 requires corrupt histories to map to DISTINCT code/layer. Your step-7 attacker pass answered "Do two causes collapse into one code? NO" - measurement contradicts it. Your own sweep lists "missing create" as a hostile case, so this is in scope.

DEFECT 2 (DoD 4 + epic rail 6, tests). The hostile sweep asserts nothing but "it did not succeed" - which is why defect 1 stayed invisible. See issues.

- Real store, real reduceGraphRevision seeding, zero local hashing, delegation pinned by the IDENTITY_CONFLICT test.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: I drafted a plan for this task once before (ownership refused the submission -- it belonged to architect-f956ffe1 then), and this replan is BETTER than that draft in three specific ways because the producers have since landed. (1) The old draft had the body record canonicalise and hash the snapshot itself; that is now forbidden and unnecessary -- encodeGraphContent is the only lawful route to a graphContentHash (the scheduler root comment says exactly this and withholds the raw mechanics), so the body record stores the codec's canonical BYTES and the read side re-validates through decodeGraphContent, whose digest check is the integrity authority. (2) The old draft had the projection fold lifecycle events with locally-enforced ordering/duplicate rules; task-ee27ed7c landed replayGraphRevisionEvents with snapshotted input, idempotent redelivery, identity-conflict refusal and no-partial-state -- so the projection DELEGATES and surfaces core codes rather than reimplementing rules, which also kills a whole class of drift. (3) The old draft could not name the structural/content identity split; now the result carries BOTH graphContentHash and snapshotIdentity and the accepted control asserts they differ, pinning dec-64b2391c at the consumer. REJECTED: (a) storing decoded content JSON instead of canonical bytes -- a second serialisation invites a second identity; (b) accepting raw content fields at putGraphBody -- recreates the mint-your-own-hash seam; (c) a single combined module -- body record and lifecycle fold have separate refusal vocabularies and would breach the per-file line target; (d) waiting for a durable graph-revision event writer -- none exists in production yet, and this task's contract is the read/persist seam; tests seed through reduceGraphRevision, the same way the replay surface's own suite does.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured at HEAD 8222b9e. REPLAY: packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-replay.ts:211 replayGraphRevisionEvents(history: unknown) -> GraphRevisionReplayResult; root-exported at packages/core/src/index.ts:109 with GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_CODES and result types; admissible() enforces exact event keys per kind; byte-identical redelivery ignored; same-version-different-bytes -> GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_IDENTITY_CONFLICT; missing create -> GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_MISSING_CREATE; refusals carry code+layer, never partial state. CONTENT: packages/scheduler root exports encodeGraphContent(content, policyOverride?) and decodeGraphContent(input) (index.ts:90-91); GraphContent = {schemaVersion, graphContentHash (all seven design-197 fields, lowercase hex64 -- the spelling @moe/core's revision gate requires), snapshotIdentity (structure-only, documented never equal), content: GraphRevisionContent, bytes}; decodeGraphContent refuses GRAPH_CONTENT_NOT_BYTES / TOO_LARGE / digest mismatch etc. from the frozen GRAPH_CONTENT_ISSUE_CODES over three frozen layers. GraphRevisionState (core contract :122) carries boundHashes/goalRef/graphContentHash/graphEpoch/lifecycle/planHash/revisionId/submissionRef/version; graphEpoch is a bound reference to the goal-owned epoch -- report, never compute. NOTHING writes graph-revision events in production yet (grep: zero non-test writers), so tests seed via reduceGraphRevision. apps/daemon/src/planning/ already exists (approval-activation, approval-gate, planning-services) -- the new modules sit beside them. apps/daemon/package.json already declares @moe/core, @moe/scheduler, @moe/store; step 1 still proves the edges with a compiled bare-specifier probe because a manifest line is not a resolution proof. A new .ts module needs its one-line .js bridge.
planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is identity theatre: a projection that returns content whose hash was never re-checked is authority-shaped without being authoritative. The design here routes ALL integrity through decodeGraphContent -- drill 2 proves the gate is load-bearing, and the accepted control asserts graphContentHash !== snapshotIdentity so the two-hash confusion (the exact failure dec-64b2391c was raised to prevent, still easy because a structural value once wore the content name) cannot re-enter through this consumer. Second, split-brain: two ACTIVE revisions must refuse, never disambiguate by epoch or recency -- picking a winner grants authority during precisely the condition the projection exists to detect. Third, silent local lifecycle rules: if the projection reimplements ordering/duplicate handling instead of delegating to replayGraphRevisionEvents, the two drift and the tests police the copy; drill 3 forces the delegation to be real. Fourth, hand-written event literals in tests let the projection pass against shapes production never writes -- seed through reduceGraphRevision only. Fifth, distinct causes need distinct codes: no-active, multiple-active, replay-refused, body-absent, body-corrupt are five failures; collapsing any two makes a later guard change invisible. Sixth, close every store handle on every path including refusals; a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker. Seventh, consumers (c4b80778, eacea969, 32c1ba45) are all BLOCKED -- name them as the consumer edge honestly rather than implying a live call site. Finally, the shared worktree rules: restore drills by re-editing, commit by explicit pathspec only.

issues.description: enumerateAggregateIds discovers aggregates ONLY by the GraphRevisionCreated event, so an aggregate whose create event is absent is never replayed. Probe over a real store: empty project, DRAFT-only project, and a create-less-but-ACTIVATED history all return the SAME refusal - code=ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT layer=ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION sourceLayer=null sourceCode=null. DoD 2 requires a corrupt history to map to a DISTINCT code/layer, not to the answer a clean empty project gives.

Fix direction: enumerate by a means a create-less history cannot escape. store.readEventsAfter(cursor, limit) exists and lets you keep every aggregateId matching the graph-revision:<projectId>: prefix; enumerating on all graph-revision event kinds also works. The create-less aggregate then reaches replayGraphRevisionEvents and surfaces GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_MISSING_CREATE with sourceLayer=CORE_GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY. Add a test asserting it differs from ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT.

The hostile sweep asserts only read.ok===false, read.layer===ACTIVE_GRAPH_PROJECTION_LAYER and typeof read.code==='string'. The layer assertion is VACUOUS: refuse() at active-graph-projection.ts:100 hardcodes layer on every refusal, so it can never hold another value. Net, the only live assertion is 'it did not succeed' - exactly what epic rail 6 and DoD 4 ('assert exact refusal code and layer') forbid, and two layers can refuse here.

Codes the sweep leaves unpinned - three codes, two layers: 'missing create' -> ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT / sourceLayer=null; 'reversed' -> GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_MISSING_CREATE / sourceLayer=CORE_GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY; 'activation before submission' -> GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY_VERSION_BREAK / sourceLayer=CORE_GRAPH_REVISION_REPLAY. Carry expected code AND sourceLayer per case-table entry and assert both. Keep the nonzero-case-count assertion.

Re-drill before completing. Drill A: make collectActive swallow the replay refusal and skip the aggregate - the sweep must go RED on a CODE assertion, not on ok===false alone; if it stays green the sweep is still detached from its subject. Drill B: after the enumeration fix, revert enumeration to create-event-only - the new create-less test must go RED on its code assertion. A drill that reddens by crashing or on another assertion proves nothing.

Your own sweep lists "missing create" as a hostile case, so this is in scope.
